result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_trails()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count all trails (walks with distinct edges) from source to target. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19394-L19535){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_trails( source, target, max_trails=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A *trail* is a walk where all edges are distinct, but nodes may repeat. This is different from: - *path*: no repeated nodes or edges (most restrictive) - *trail*: no repeated edges, but nodes may repeat - *walk*: nodes and edges may repeat freely (least restrictive) Uses iterative depth-first search with edge tracking. Can grow exponentially for dense graphs, so use `max_trails=` parameter to limit computation. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source node ID (int) or label (str). [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Target node ID (int) or label (str). [max_trails]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of trails to count before stopping. If `None`, counts all trails. If exceeded, returns `None`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of distinct trails from source to target. Returns `None` if `max_trails=` exceeded. Returns `1` if source == target (trivial empty trail). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If source or target node not found in graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} **Complexity**: - Time: O(trails × avg_trail_length) - exponential in worst case - Space: O(edges) per trail in exploration stack **Growth Rate**: - triangle (3 nodes): ~2 trails - complete K4 (4 nodes): ~12 trails - complete K5 (5 nodes): ~100+ trails - can easily exceed millions for dense graphs **Implementation**: - uses iterative DFS with explicit stack (avoids recursion limits) - tracks visited edges (not nodes) to allow node revisiting - for undirected graphs, edges are bidirectional ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a triangle `A -- B -- C -- A`, there are two distinct trails from `A` to `C`: the direct edge, and the longer route through `B`: ::: {#827f2e7c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) count = graph.count_trails("A", "C") # Returns 2 (trails: A->C and A->B->C) count ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Node IDs work just as well as labels: ::: {#5b332274 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_node(label="B") graph.add_edge("A", "B") a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") # Returns 1 (a single trail A->B) graph.count_trails(a_id, b_id) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Real-world graphs can have an enormous number of trails, so `max_trails` caps the search and returns `None` once the limit is exceeded rather than running indefinitely: ::: {#a12b1b9d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} G = ec.karate_club() node_ids = list(G.get_node_ids()) first_node = node_ids[0] last_node = node_ids[-1] count = G.count_trails(first_node, last_node, max_trails=10000) # None means more than 10,000 trails exist between these two nodes count is None ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Adding a shortcut edge `B -> D` gives two trails between `A` and `D` that use different edges, unlike simple paths which are restricted to non-repeated nodes: ::: {#9db3e49f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") .add_edge("B", "D") # Shortcut ) # Returns 2 (A->B->D and A->B->C->D) graph.count_trails("A", "D") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
